title: Randomized controlled clinical study on bone preservation after tooth extractions with a collagen cone covered with a resorbable magnesium barrier membrane compared to a control group.
summary:
Abstract: The aim of the study is to compare the use of a porcine collagen cone covered with a resorbable magnesium barrier membrane, which is placed in an empty socket immediately after tooth extraction (test group), with tooth extraction in which only a collagen cone is inserted without any further measures (control group). The difference in the reduction of bone loss after tooth extraction between a control and a test group is examined.
Bone preservation is an important parameter for a successful implant treatment.
The hypothesis is that there is a difference in bone preservation in the bucco-oral and mesio-distal direction between the alveoli in the test group (socket preservation) and healing of the alveoli without further measures. It is expected that the volume of the bone will be better preserved by inserting a collagen cone and using a resorbable barrier membrane.

interventions.name:
Test group:
In 20 patients, a collagen cone made from porcine dermis (collacone, botiss biomaterials GmbH, Zossen, Germany) is inserted into the extraction socket after extraction. The socket is also covered with a resorbable magnesium barrier membrane (NOVAMag mebrane, botiss biomaterials GmbH, Zo

Control group:
In 20 patients, wound healing will occur after the insertion of a collagen cone (collacone, botiss biomaterials GmbH, Zossen, Germany) without any further measures.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who require the extraction of at least one tooth in the upper jaw (15-25). The extraction may be indicated for periodontal reasons or destruction of the tooth due to caries or trauma, which preclude the preservation of the tooth. The missing tooth should be restored with an implant.
A requirement for inclusion in the patient group is that a tooth or an existing implant is present in the immediate vicinity of the tooth to be extracted.
Exclusion criteria:
• Persons under 18 or legally incompetent persons
• Recognizable primary additional need for augmentation
• Insertion of the implant with an implant drilling template not possible (insufficient mouth opening).
• Heavy smokers (more than 10 cigs/day)
• Taking bisphosphonates
• Pregnant
• Alcohol or drug addicts
• Patients with an infectious disease such as hepatitis or HIV/AIDS
• Patients with uncontrolled severe diabetes mellitus. The long-term blood sugar level, HbA1c, must be below 6.7%.
